key_insight: PHO-Agents combines structured EHR modeling with multi-agent LLM reasoning to improve health outcome prediction and explanation quality.
clinical_relevance: This hybrid approach may help support clinical decision-making by producing more accurate predictions with interpretable, guideline-informed reasoning.
method: Encodes longitudinal EHR sequences into attention-based patient representations and initial risk logits.
Uses a data agent to turn EHR signals into patient summaries, plus retrieval, research, and doctor agents to assess the case.
Fuses EHR model outputs with LLM agent analyses to generate final predictions and explanation reports.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three real-world cohorts (AKI mortality, CKD-related AKI onset, and ICI-related adverse events), it outperformed single-agent and multi-agent LLM baselines, with AKI PR-AUC 90.20 ± 2.07 vs 56.46 ± 2.98 for the best single-agent baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable retrieval and careful integration of LLM reasoning, so performance and interpretability may vary across settings and require prospective validation.
paper_title: PHO-Agents: A Large Language Model Powered Multi-Agent System for Predicting Health Outcomes
